subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Solar Flares and Coronal Mass Ejections
description: A 60-second lesson on Solar Flares and Coronal Mass Ejections.

hook.text: Solar flares release bursts of radiation in minutes. Coronal mass ejections hurl billions of tons of plasma into space.

buildup.text: Both are caused by twisted magnetic field lines that snap and reconnect. The energy release is sudden and enormous.

discovery.text: The Carrington Event of 1859 was the strongest solar storm on record. It sparked auroras at the equator and fried telegraph wires.

twist.text: A Carrington-level event today could disable satellites, power grids, and communications worldwide for weeks or months.

climax.text: In May 2024, the strongest geomagnetic storm in 20 years hit Earth. Auroras were seen from places that rarely see them.

punchline.text: Solar tantrums reach Earth in hours. Our technology makes us more vulnerable than ever.

quiz.question: What would happen if a Carrington-level solar storm hit Earth today?
options: It could disable satellites, power grids, and communications worldwide for weeks
It would cool the Earth significantly by blocking sunlight
It would have no effect due to modern technology and shielding

details.summary: Solar flares are intense bursts of radiation from the Sun's surface caused by magnetic field reconnection, while coronal mass ejections (CMEs) hurl billions of tons of magnetized plasma into space.
details.whyItMatters: Space weather from the Sun directly affects modern technology and infrastructure. Understanding solar flares and CMEs is critical for protecting satellites, power systems, and astronaut safety.
takeaways: Solar flares are intense radiation bursts from magnetic reconnection
CMEs hurl billions of tons of plasma into space
They cause geomagnetic storms affecting technology on Earth

faq.question: What was the worst solar storm in recorded history?
faq.answer: The Carrington Event of 1859. A massive CME hit Earth, causing auroras visible near the equator and frying telegraph systems worldwide — some operators received electric shocks. A similar event today could cause trillions of dollars in damage to power grids and satellites.

faq.question: Can solar storms be predicted?
faq.answer: Partially. Solar observatories like the Solar Dynamics Observatory monitor the Sun continuously. Flares can be detected instantly via light speed, but CMEs take 1-3 days to reach Earth, providing some warning.
